title: WPSS/896/2023 of DEEKSHA JOSHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 896 of 2023
Deeksha Joshi and Others ......Petitioners
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Another ..... Respondent
Mr. Devesh Upreti, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Additional C.S.C. for the State.

Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 By means of the instant petition, the
petitioners seek the following reliefs:-
"(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus commanding the
respondents not to disturb the
appointment/engagement of the
petitioners as guest teachers in their
present working schools, either by
transfer/promotion of working teachers
or directly recruited teachers, until all
the vacant posts of Assistant Teacher
(LT) & Lecturers are filled up.
(ii) Issue any other writ, order or direction,
which in the interest of justice and
under the circumstances of the case the
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper.
(iii) Award the cost of the petition to the
petitioners"

2
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. It is the case of the petitioners that the
petitioner nos. 1 to 7 are lecturers and petitioner no.8
is Assistant Teacher LT Grade, working as Guest
teachers in the different Government Inter Colleges.
Their appointment is regulated by the Government
Order dated 25.05.2016. Another Government Order
dated 16.12.2020 provides that if any guest teacher is
affected by appointment/posting of regular teacher, in
such eventuality, after getting options from the
affected guest teacher, he/she shall be adjusted in
accordance with his/her merit, according to the
options given by such guest teacher, preferably in the
same District and in case of non availability of
vacancies of the same subject in the same District,
such guest teacher may be adjusted in the same
region.
4. According to the petitioners, they came to
know that the respondents have prepared a transfer
list of lecturers and promotion list of Assistant
Teachers for promoting them as lecturers, in the post
of Lecturers, where the petitioners are presently
posted. According to the petitioners, there are several

3
other schools, where positions are vacant. Therefore,
the respondents authority may be directed not to
disturb the petitioners from their present place of
posting unless the vacant posts in other schools are
filled up.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners would
submit that the petitioners are guest teachers. The
respondent authorities may appoint regular teachers.
It is submitted that there are various other vacant
posts, against which regular appointment can be made
and until all the vacancies are filled up, the petitioners
should not be disturbed in terms of their engagement
in the particular school, where they are working now.
6. In support of his contention, learned
counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance on the
principle of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the case of Rajesh Dhami & Others, . Vs. The
State of Uttarakhand and Others, Civil Appeal Nos.
284-286 of 2020. He would refer to directions (iv) & (v)
of the judgment in the case of Rajesh Dhami (surpa).
7. In the case of Rajesh Dhami (supra),
under directions (iv) & (v), the Hon'ble Supreme Court
directed as hereunder:-

4
(iv) In the interregnum period, to take care of the
exigency, the State Government has gone through a
process of selecting adhoc/guest teachers which are
stated to be 4076 lecturers and 834 licenced
teachers. This process can go ahead, of course
making it clear that they will have no right to
regularisation or appointments and thus only an
adhoc arrangement till the vacancies are filled up.
(v) The case of the appellants before us is that they
were appointed as ad hoc teachers but have not
been functioning now since 31st March, 2018. Their
appointment took place in 2015. It is also not
disputed before us that even after the newly selected
guest teachers are appointed, still there are
vacancies remaining and thus the appellants and all
similarly situated persons can also be
accommodated conveniently. Needless to say that
what applies to the new persons so appointed will
equally apply to them for their terms of
appointment.
8. It is the case of the petitioner that the
appointment of the guest teachers has been made
pursuant to Government Order dated 25.05.2016,
which is Annexure No.1 to the writ petition. The
Clause 2 of this Government Order itself reveals that
in case of regular appointment, the guest teachers may
be shifted to at any other place.
9. The petitioners cannot claim that they
should not be disturbed unless all the vacancies
everywhere are filled up. The petitioners can not claim
against the terms and conditions of the Government

5
Order dated 25.05.2016 (its clause 2 particularly).
Such directions may not be issued. Therefore, this
Court does not see any reason to entertain the writ
petition. Accordingly, the writ petition deserves to be
dismissed at the stage of admission itself.
10. The writ petition is dismissed in in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 22.06.2023
